content.thinking:
Okay, I've just triggered the UI to switch the session provider to Claude‑code and clicked the start button. The preview eval returned the string “launching claude-code”, which means the browser has begun initializing the interactive session. However, the actual Claude‑code TUI runs inside a container that takes a moment to spin up and connect to the front‑end. In previous steps, after launching the session I always inserted a short pause before trying to interact with the terminal, because the WebSocket connection isn't ready immediately and any commands sent too early just get lost or produce “no data” logs.

Looking at the earlier timing test, I saw that after starting the server I had to wait several seconds (the ws connection only became active after a few seconds, and then there were long idle periods). The last Bash command I used was a `sleep 3 && uv run …` to give the server time to start before running the test script. Now that I've just launched the UI session, I need a similar delay, but a bit longer because the UI also needs to load the new view, render the provider segment, and the backend container must spin up the Claude‑code process.

I don't need to poll or check any state yet; a simple sleep is sufficient. The next step after the wait will be to capture the output of the TUI or send a command to it, so I should give it enough time to become fully ready. Based on the previous behavior, a wait of around 15–20 seconds should be safe. I'll choose 18 seconds to be comfortably within the 30‑second timeout I set for the Bash tool, ensuring the container and TUI have ample time to initialize without exceeding the limit.

Thus, the next action is to run a Bash command that sleeps for 18 seconds, with a description indicating it's to wait for the container and Claude TUI, and a timeout of 30 000 ms.

arguments.description: Wait for container and claude TUI
